title: The Master's Face
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji stepped into the depths of the Forbidden Grounds, a terrifying aura that surpassed the Eye of Heavenly Mandate slowly awakened from the depths of the Dragon Vein—a existence that even the Tianji Record dared not to glimpse.

text.content: The entrance to the Forbidden Grounds gaped like a monstrous maw devouring all things, with dark fog churning with eerie purple light. Chen Ji halted his steps as he recognized the face emerging from the darkness—a face he believed had long since dispersed into spiritual oblivion. Mo Xiansheng, still in his blue robes, as elegant as ever, but the soul fire surrounding him was dimmer by a third compared to memory, as if it might extinguish at any moment between heaven and earth. "Master?" Chen Ji's voice seemed particularly jarring in the silence. He unconsciously gripped the Tianji Record Fragment in his sleeve, his knuckles whitening from the strain.

dialogue.content: "Coming uninvited is my rudeness, Master. Chen Ji, you cannot enter this forbidden place." Mo Xiansheng's voice remained gentle, yet carried an indescribable heaviness. He raised his hand in a seemingly gentle gesture of restraint, but Chen Ji felt the surrounding spiritual energy suddenly solidify, as if an invisible shackle had locked him in place.

text.content: Chen Ji's eyes flickered as he rapidly calculated in his heart. Mo Xiansheng's residual soul should have been sleeping on the first page of the Tianji Record, so why could it appear independently here? More importantly, the timing of his obstruction was too precise—exactly the moment before Chen Ji was about to step into the Dragon Vein's core. This was by no means coincidence. "If Master truly has my best interests at heart," Chen Ji slowly spoke, his tonecalm得近乎cold, "why not rest peacefully within the Tianji Record? Why block my path here instead?"

dialogue.content: Upon hearing this, a complex expression crossed Mo Xiansheng's face—seemingly bitter, seemingly helpless. "You doubt me." This was not a question, but a statement. He sighed lightly, his soul fire flickering slightly. "Very well, since things have come to this, there are some things you truly should know." He met Chen Ji's gaze directly, his eyes deep as an abyss. "Do you know who the original master of the Tianji Record was?"

choice.prompt: Facing Mo Xiansheng's profound question, how should Chen Ji respond?

choices.description: Press Mo Xiansheng about his identity with a cold,硬姿态, leaving no room for maneuver
choices.visible_reward: Fastest way to obtain the truth
choices.risk_hint: If Mo Xiansheng has ulterior motives, may result in a complete fallout

text.content: Chen Ji let out a cold laugh, his eyes flashing with sharp light. "Why must Master beat around the bush? The residual soul guardian on the first page of the Tianji Record—" he articulated each word deliberately, "or perhaps—the original first holder?" The moment his words fell, the fog at the entrance of the Forbidden Grounds seemed to freeze. Mo Xiansheng's expression finally cracked, and an intense sharpness flickered in those always-gentle eyes that Chen Ji had never witnessed before.

choices.text: Retreat to Advance, Testing the Waters
choices.description: Pretend to comply while secretly observing Mo Xiansheng's flaws, seeking opportunities to escape or counter
choices.visible_cost: May delay the timing for entering the Forbidden Grounds
choices.visible_reward: Preserve trump cards without revealing true intentions
choices.risk_hint: If Mo Xiansheng is also well-versed in strategy, may be seen through

text.content: Chen Ji lowered his eyes, completely concealing that flash of sharpness. He slightly bowed, his voice returning to its usual respectful tone: "Your disciple was presumptuous, please instruct me, Master." Mo Xiansheng gazed at him for a moment, a meaningful smile flickering in his eyes. "This child of mine has learned to hide his thoughts better than before." He stepped forward, his residual soul form flickering in the fog. "Since you wish to know, Master will tell you a tale of dust-laden past."

dialogue.content: "Three hundred years ago, the holder of the Tianji Record was not Chen Xuan, but someone else." Mo Xiansheng's voice was low, as if recounting an ancient secret. "That person, in pursuit of a higher Heavenly Mandate, split and sealed the Tianji Record, while he himself transformed into the Dragon Vein, eternally guarding this place." He paused, his gaze falling on Chen Ji's hand gripping the fragment tightly. "Chen Xuan was merely one of the successors he chose. And I—" the soul fire shuddered violently, "I was the one who was eliminated."

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. Three hundred years of past events—this amount of information far exceeded his estimates. If what Mo Xiansheng said was true, then the layout of the Tianji Record had been in motion for at least three hundred years, and he was merely a piece on this grand chessboard. This realization sent a chill down his spine. "Since Master was the eliminated one," he suppressed the tumultuous waves in his heart, "why help me? Why remain within the Tianji Record?"

dialogue.content: Mo Xiansheng suddenly laughed—that smile carried an indescribable sorrow and mockery. "Because you are my only hope." He stepped forward, his soul fire surging violently, casting his face in alternating light and shadow. "The Eye of Heavenly Mandate has chosen you, but only wants to use you as the next sacrifice. And what I intend to do—" he suddenly raised his hand, a profound rune shooting from his fingertips, directly aimed at Chen Ji's Brow Center, "is to grant you the ability to overturn the chessboard before you become a sacrifice!"

choice.prompt: Mo Xiansheng suddenly made his move, a mysterious rune heading straight for his Brow Center. What choice should Chen Ji make?

choices.description: Evade the rune with movement technique, expressing distrust in the most intense manner
choices.visible_reward: Maintain the initiative, not be controlled by others
choices.risk_hint: If the talisman contains tracking effects, there is no escape

text.content: Chen Ji surged backward, his toes plowing two deep grooves into the ground. Yet the talisman seemed to possess eyes, bypassing his evasive trajectory and precisely adhering to his Brow Center. In that instant, a scorching force flooded into his Mental Sea, Chen Ji felt his vision darken, countless unfamiliar scenes flickering past like a carousel—those were chapters the Tianji Record had never revealed, true forbidden secrets.

choices.description: Choosing to trust Mo Xiansheng, allowing the talisman to enter his body to obtain inheritance information
choices.visible_reward: Acquire deeper knowledge of the Tianji Record
choices.risk_hint: If Mo Xiansheng is treacherous, it may be irretrievable doom

text.content: Chen Ji did not dodge. He let the talisman sink into his Brow Center, the searing pain instantly spreading through his entire body. After a moment, he saw it—the true complete picture of the Tianji Record, not fragments, but the complete Heavenly Dao trajectory. And at the end of those trajectories, there was an existence vaster and more terrifying than the Heavenly Dao's Eye slowly opening its eyes. "That is..." Chen Ji cried out, his voice trembling almost incoherently.

dialogue.content: "The Heart of the Dragon Vein," Mo Xiansheng's voice came from afar, carrying unprecedented solemnity. "You thought the Heavenly Dao's Eye was the final enemy? You're wrong." He waved his hand, and those visions abruptly scattered. Chen Ji returned to reality, yet discovered he was drenched in cold sweat. "The Heavenly Dao's Eye is merely that thing's eyes and ears, and what sleeps deep within the Dragon Vein—" He took a deep breath. "Is the true Heavenly Dao itself. The ultimate secret of the Tianji Record is not to foresee the future, but—"

text.content: Chen Ji stared intently at Mo Xiansheng, his mind racing to integrate all the information. The first master of the Tianji Record had transformed into the Dragon Vein, the Heavenly Dao's Eye was merely an informant, there was an even more terrifying existence deep in the Dragon Vein... If these pieces of information were true, the entire cultivation world's structure would be completely overturned. And he, Chen Ji, had all along been caught in a vortex beyond imagination. "Since Master knows all this," he asked deeply, "why not tell me directly back then? Why wait until today?"

dialogue.content: Mo Xiansheng's expression suddenly dimmed, his soul flame flickering more and more weakly. "Because the timing wasn't right." He turned around, his back facing Chen Ji, his voice carrying a hint of weariness. "Your cultivation wasn't sufficient. Knowing too much would only bring disaster. And now—" He tilted his head, his gaze sweeping across the swirling violet-black mist in the depths of the forbidden grounds. "The Dragon Vein is changing, that thing seems to have sensed the fluctuations of the Tianji Record. If you insist on entering, perhaps..." He didn't finish, but the implication was clear.

choice.prompt: Faced with Mo Xiansheng's warning, Chen Ji must make a choice: venture deeper into the forbidden grounds or temporarily retreat?

choices.description: Since we've come this far, never retreat, even if the true Heavenly Dao itself lies ahead
choices.visible_cost: May confront an existence beyond the Heavenly Dao's Eye
choices.visible_reward: Obtain the secrets of the Dragon Vein's core, possibly completely rewriting fate
choices.risk_hint: Extremely high risk, possibly no return

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, his hesitation gradually replaced by determination. He bowed deeply to Mo Xiansheng, his voice calm yet firm: "Thank you for the warning, Master, but some things cannot be avoided. Chen Nian is still in the Holy Sect's hands, the Heavenly Dao's Eye's chess game has already been played—I if I don't actively enter the game, I can only wait to be eliminated." He raised his head, meeting Mo Xiansheng's gaze. "Since Master says I am the only hope, then this hope, I shall strive for with my own hands."

choices.description: Acknowledge insufficient strength, withdraw from the forbidden grounds first, plan carefully
choices.risk_hint: The Dragon Vein's anomalies may continue to worsen

text.content: Chen Ji remained silent for a long while before finally stepping back slowly. 'You're right, Master. Rashly sending oneself to death isn't a wise move.' He lowered his eyes, hiding the reluctance in his gaze. 'There will be other ways to handle Chen Nian's matter, and the secrets of the Tianji Record don't need to be rushed.' He raised his head again, eyes burning intensely. 'But I have one condition—Master must tell me everything you know, without reservation. This time, I refuse to be a blind chess piece.'

dialogue.content: Mo Xiansheng gazed at Chen Ji for a long moment, a flicker of approval crossing his eyes. 'Very well.' He nodded, and the soul flames around him suddenly condensed into an ancient jade slip, drifting into Chen Ji's hands. 'This contains all the truths I know, including... the weaknesses of the Heavenly Eye.' His form began to grow translucent, as if he might dissipate at any moment. 'But there is one thing I must warn you—'

text.content: The moment Chen Ji received the jade slip, a torrent of information flooded into his mind. The contents far exceeded his imagination—the true origin of the Tianji Record, the shocking secrets from three hundred years ago, and a possibility he had never contemplated: the complete form of the Tianji Record was actually a key.

dialogue.content: 'A key to open what?' Chen Ji pressed. Mo Xiansheng's form had faded until it was almost invisible, only his eyes still bright. 'A key to open—' His voice faltered, as if he had exhausted his final strength. '—let that thing descend completely...' Before the words finished, the soul flames abruptly extinguished, and Mo Xiansheng's form completely dissolved into the mist.

text.content: Silence returned to the entrance of the Forbidden Grounds. Chen Ji stood alone, the warm jade slip in his hand, waves of indescribable complexity churning in his heart. Mo Xiansheng's words were like a heavy hammer, shattering his original understanding. The Tianji Record was not an oracle of destiny, but a key to unleashing catastrophe—then what were all his years of persistence worth? Those Heavenly Fate values consumed, those elaborate chess games carefully arranged—were they from the start nothing but a joke?

Just then, the Tianji Record Fragment hidden in his sleeve suddenly vibrated violently. A familiar yet strange aura emerged from the depths of the Forbidden Grounds, creating some诡异的 resonance with the fragment. Chen Ji looked down to see the Tianji runes on the fragment reorganizing in a way he had never witnessed before, as if responding to some kind of summoning. And the source of that summoning was precisely the core of the Dragon Vein—that place where existed the entity Mo Xiansheng had called even more terrifying than the Heavenly Eye.

dialogue.content: 'Heh.' Chen Ji suddenly laughed lightly, that laugh sounding particularly abrupt at the silent entrance of the Forbidden Grounds. He raised his head to look at the swirling purple-black mist ahead, his eyes flashing sharply: 'Want me to be your key? Let's see if you have the ability to unlock me.' He tucked the jade slip into his chest and strode toward the depths of the Forbidden Grounds, his back resolute and solitary.

text.content: The process of venturing deeper into the Forbidden Grounds was far more perilous than Chen Ji had anticipated. Everywhere were collapsed ruins and twisted Spiritual Energy, the air thick with decay and the scent of blood. He dared not easily use the Tianji Record's foresight ability—Mo Xiansheng's warning still echoed in his ears; the consumption of Heavenly Fate values was minor, but disturbing that slumbering existence was the real concern. However, just as he advanced carefully, a familiar female voice suddenly came from ahead: 'Chen Ji?'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji froze instantly, his hand already pressing against the short blade hidden in his sleeve. The figure emerged from the mist—clad in black纱, with a blood-colored mark between her brows—the Demon Path Holy Sect's Saint Maiden, Ye Qing. Her expression was graver than when they last met, and the demonic mist around her had also faded considerably. 'What are you doing here?' Chen Ji didn't relax his vigilance. 'The aura of this Forbidden Grounds will expose your position—if the Holy Sect learns of our cooperation...'

Ye Qing shook her head, quickly walking to Chen Ji's side, lowering her voice: 'Precisely because of this, I must come to warn you.' She glanced back at the darkness behind her, a flicker of fear in her eyes. 'The Holy Sect already knows about the Dragon Vein's mutation—what they've sent isn't just me—' She took a deep breath. 'Ling Yuan, the old Sect Master, is also on his way. And from what I know, he's also brought a forbidden artifact specifically designed to counter the Tianji Record.'

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly. Ling Yuan—that old fox who superficially sheltered him but secretly harbored malicious intentions—had actually pursued him at this critical moment. More troublesome was that forbidden artifact—he didn't know what it was, but anything that would make Ye Qing specifically come to warn him was certainly no ordinary object. 'Seems the waters in this Forbidden Grounds run deeper than I imagined.' Chen Ji murmured to himself, yet a cold smile curved his lips. 'But that's fine too—muddy waters are where you catch big fish.'

Chen Ji hid the jade slip carefully against his body, where Mo Xiansheng's final warning still lingered in his heart. He gazed into the swirling purple-black mist深处 of the Forbidden Grounds, where something was slowly awakening—an existence older and more terrifying than the Heavenly Eye. Ling Yuan approached with an artifact to counter the Tianji Record, and the secrets of the Dragon Vein's core might be hidden within that unknown darkness. No matter what, this game of chess had reached the moment when he had no choice but to make his move.
